title: Settings

workspace.heading: Workspace
workspace.ownersOnly: Only owners can rename the workspace.
workspace.description: The name and basic settings of this workspace.
workspace.nameDescription: Shown in the sidebar, in invitations and in emails.

export.heading: Export
export.title: Export workspace
export.description: Download every page you can see as a ZIP: pages as Markdown, databases as CSV, and the files they show. Pages in the trash are left out; templates are kept in a Templates folder.
export.disabled: Export is turned off for this workspace in Settings → Security.

members.heading: Members
members.description: Members can see and edit every page unless its sharing is restricted; guests see only pages shared with them. Owners can also manage members.

joinLink.heading: Add members with a link
joinLink.descriptionOn: Anyone who opens this link and signs in joins as a member, or with the role of a pending invitation for their email. Only owners can see it.
joinLink.descriptionOff: Turn on a link that anyone can use to join this workspace as a member.
joinLink.regenerateBody: The current link stops working right away. People who already joined keep their access.
joinLink.descriptionAsks: Anyone who opens this link and signs in asks to join, and an owner approves each request. People with a pending invitation join right away. Only owners can see it.

members.transferBody: {name} becomes an owner and you become a member. Only an owner can make you an owner again.
members.leaveBody: You lose access to its pages. Pages only you could manage pass to an owner. An owner can add you again.
members.removeBody: {name} loses access to this workspace right away, including in open pages and connected apps. Pages only they could manage pass to you.
members.expired: Link expired. Invite again for a new one.

add.title: Add members
add.description: People with an account are added right away. Everyone else gets an invitation link.
add.count: {count, plural, =0 {Separate addresses with commas, spaces or new lines. Up to 50 at a time.} one {# address} other {# addresses}}
add.linkValidity: Invitation links work for 7 days and only for the invited email address.
add.descriptionAsks: An owner approves each address before anyone is added or invited.
add.requestedNote: Owners see your request in Settings > Members. Invitations go out once they approve.

guests.heading: Guests
guests.description: Guests are people from outside the workspace who see only the pages shared with them. See what each guest can open, take access back, make a guest a member or remove them.
guests.descriptionMember: Guests are people from outside the workspace who see only the pages shared with them. You can take back access on pages you have full access to. Only owners can make a guest a member or remove them.
guests.count: {count, plural, =0 {No guests} one {# guest} other {# guests}}
guests.empty: No guests yet. Sharing a page with the email address of someone outside the workspace adds them as a guest.
guests.noMatches: No guests or pages match your search.
guests.pageCount: {count, plural, =0 {No pages} one {# page} other {# pages}}
guests.hidden: {count, plural, one {# more page you don't have access to} other {# more pages you don't have access to}}
guests.makeMemberBody: {name} can then open the workspace's pages like any member, not only the pages shared with them, and join teamspaces.
guests.removeBody: {name} loses access to this workspace right away, including in open pages and connected apps. Pages only they could manage pass to you.
guests.revokeBody: The invitation link stops working, and the pages shared with {email} stop waiting for them.

teamspaces.heading: Teamspaces
teamspaces.description: Teamspaces group pages and the people working on them. Everyone sees the teamspaces they are in in their sidebar. Guests are never in teamspaces; they only see pages shared with them.
teamspaces.listDescription: Manage all the teamspaces you have access to here.
teamspaces.leaveBody: Its pages leave your sidebar. You can join an open teamspace again yourself; otherwise one of its owners has to add you.
teamspaces.archiveBody: It leaves everyone's sidebar and takes no new pages. You can restore it from the archived teamspaces.

defaults.heading: Default teamspaces
defaults.description: Everyone in the workspace is in these teamspaces and can't leave them, including people who join later. There is nothing to update when someone joins. New top-level pages go to the oldest one.
defaults.empty: No default teamspaces. New top-level pages go to people's private pages.
defaults.makeBody: Everyone in the workspace, now and later, is in it and can't leave it. Its pages appear in everyone's sidebar.
defaults.removeBody: Everyone stays in it for now but can leave it, and people who join the workspace later aren't added.

creation.title: Only workspace owners can create teamspaces
creation.description: Off: owners and members can create teamspaces. Guests never can.
creation.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can change this.

groups.heading: Groups
groups.description: Groups bundle people so you can share a page with all of them or add them to a teamspace at once. Whoever joins a group gets what the group has; whoever leaves it loses it. Only owners and members can be in groups, not guests.
groups.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can create and change groups.
groups.emptyOwner: No groups yet. Create one to share pages with several people at once.
groups.memberCount: {count, plural, =0 {No members} one {# member} other {# members}}
groups.name: Name
groups.deleteBody: Its members keep the access they have on their own. What the group was given on pages and in teamspaces goes away, and open pages they can no longer see close. Pages only the group could manage pass to you.

members.title: Members of {name}
members.empty: No one is in this group yet.
members.noOneToAdd: Every owner and member of the workspace is already in this group.
members.provisionedHint: Your identity provider manages this group over SCIM. Changes made here may be undone at its next sync.

errors.nameTaken: Another group already has this name.
errors.notMember: Only owners and members of the workspace can be in its groups.
errors.accessDenied: Only workspace owners can change groups.

agents.heading: Agents
agents.description: Agents are AI helpers with instructions of their own. An automation runs one on a database’s rows: it reads only what is shared with it, changes the row and comments on it, under its own name.
agents.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can create and change agents.
agents.emptyOwner: No agents yet. Create one, or start from a template below.
agents.restoreHint: A restored agent starts paused, with nothing shared with it.
agents.aiOff: AI is off in this workspace (Settings > General), so agents don’t run.
agents.aiUnavailable: AI isn’t set up on this server, so agents don’t run.
agents.archiveBody: It stops running and loses every page shared with it. Automations that run it skip it until it’s restored. What it changed and wrote keeps its name.

form.name: Name
form.descriptionPlaceholder: What it does, in a sentence
form.instructionsPlaceholder: For example: Read the new request. Set Team to Billing for questions about money, to Support otherwise. Explain your choice in a comment.
form.instructionsHelp: What the agent does whenever it runs: what to look at, what to change, what to write. It sees only the pages shared with it.
form.activeHelp: A paused agent’s runs end without doing anything.
form.archivedNote: Restore the agent to change it.

access.description: The agent opens only these pages, and the pages and rows under them.
access.warning: Anything you share with an agent can end up in the rows it changes or the comments it writes, where everyone who can see those rows can read it.
access.empty: Nothing is shared with this agent yet.
access.hidden: {count, plural, one {# more page you can’t open is shared with it.} other {# more pages you can’t open are shared with it.}}
access.archived: An archived agent has nothing shared with it.
access.noPages: No other page you have full access to.
access.fullOnly: You can share pages you have full access to.
access.automationNote: An automation that runs this agent gives it edit access to its database when it’s saved.

runs.description: Its latest runs, kept for {days} days.
runs.noSteps: It didn’t search, read or change anything.
runs.commentHidden: Commented on a row you can’t open

reason.aiOff: AI is off in this workspace.
reason.agentDisabled: The agent was paused or archived.
reason.noAccess: The agent can’t open the row or its database.
reason.tooManyAttempts: It couldn’t start in time: the workspace’s AI allowance stayed used up.
reason.approvalTimeout: No one answered its call within a day, so nothing was sent.
reason.connectionGone: The connection that started it was removed.

runs.waiting: It waits for an owner to answer this call:

tool.declined: Its call of “{tool}” on {connection} was declined; nothing was sent
tool.redo: Its call of “{tool}” on {connection} was sent back; nothing was sent
tool.expired: Its call of “{tool}” on {connection} ran out of time; nothing was sent

templates.heading: Start from a template
templates.description: Ready-made agents for a database. Each runs on every new row; you choose the database and the properties it uses.

wizard.title: Set up {name}
wizard.chooseDatabase: Which database should it work on? You need full access to it.
wizard.noDatabases: No database you have full access to.
wizard.routerPropertiesHelp: Up to {max}. For a select or status it picks one of the options; for a person, someone of the workspace.
wizard.rulesPlaceholder: Questions about invoices or refunds: Category is Question. Anything broken: Category is Problem, Assignee is Deniz.
wizard.rulesHelp: In your own words: how to fill each property, and when.
wizard.answerPropertyHelp: A select or status it sets once it has answered, or when a person needs to step in.
wizard.needsPerson: When a person needs to step in
wizard.newOptionsNote: The new property gets the options “{answered}” and “{needsPerson}”.
wizard.flagPropertyHelp: Ticked on a new row that looks like others.
wizard.knowledgeHelp: Up to {max}, shared with the agent to view. It answers only from these pages.
wizard.noPages: No page you have full access to.
wizard.name: Agent name
wizard.summary: Creating it adds the agent and an automation on {database} that runs it on every new row. The agent gets edit access to {database}.
wizard.summaryPages: The pages you chose are shared with it to view.

errors.tooMany: A workspace can have at most {max} agents.
errors.archived: Restore the agent to change it.
errors.notAPage: This page can’t be shared with the agent: you need full access to it.
errors.accessDenied: Only workspace owners can change agents.

reasons.name: Give the agent a name.
reasons.icon: An agent’s icon is an emoji.
reasons.level: An agent can view, comment on or edit a page.
reasons.database: Choose a database of this workspace.
reasons.property: Choose properties of the right type.
reasons.option: Choose two different options of the property.

connections.description: The tools of each connection this agent may use. Tools that only read run at once; any other waits for an owner’s approval every time the agent calls it.
connections.empty: No connections yet. Owners add them in <link>Settings › Connections</link>.
connections.notReady: This connection isn’t ready (it needs a sign-in or fails), so the agent can’t use its tools for now.

analytics.description: How much people edited in this workspace, counted from page history and each page's latest change. Nothing extra is tracked. Only owners see this.
analytics.howCounted: An edit is a saved version of a page (at most one every 10 minutes while someone types, and one before each app, AI or restore change) or a change page history doesn't keep, such as a row's values.
analytics.peopleDescription: Guests are listed with their edits but don't count as active members.
analytics.pagesDescription: Pages you can't open are counted but not named.
analytics.exportPeople: Download edits per person as CSV
analytics.exportPages: Download most edited pages as CSV

preferences.description: Your account's preferences: how Leafdesk looks in this browser and which emails you get.

language.heading: Language
language.label: Interface language
language.note: This setting applies to this browser only. Emails to you are in the language you last picked or signed in with.

leaveWorkspace.title: Leave workspace
leaveWorkspace.description: You're a guest here and see only the pages shared with you. Leaving removes that access.

copyManually: Copying isn't available here. Select the text and press Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac).

connectedApps.revokeError: Could not revoke access. Try again.

mcp.heading: Connect an AI assistant
mcp.description: Leafdesk has a built-in MCP server. Assistants that support remote MCP servers can search, read and edit your pages and databases after you sign in and approve access. Every edit an assistant makes is saved to page history first, so you can undo it.

claude.title: Claude
claude.body: Open Settings, then Connectors, choose Add custom connector and paste the server URL. Claude opens Leafdesk in your browser so you can sign in and allow access.

claudeCode.title: Claude Code
claudeCode.body: Run this in a terminal, then use /mcp inside Claude Code to sign in.

codex.title: Codex
codex.body: Run this in a terminal. Codex sees that Leafdesk uses OAuth and opens your browser so you can sign in and allow access; if that window gets closed, run codex mcp login leafdesk. Update Codex first: older versions can't finish signing in.

other.title: Other MCP clients
other.body: Add a remote server with the Streamable HTTP transport and the URL above. The client discovers sign-in through standard OAuth 2.1 metadata; it can register itself automatically or use a client ID metadata document. Choose read-only access on the approval screen if the client should not edit anything.

errors.alreadyMember: This person is already a member.
errors.notMember: This person is not a member.
errors.lastOwner: A workspace needs at least one owner.
errors.lastOwnerRemove: A workspace needs at least one owner. Make someone else an owner first.
errors.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can do this.
errors.invitationInvalid: This invitation is invalid or has expired.
errors.invitationEmailMismatch: This invitation is for a different email address.
errors.emailRequired: Enter at least one email address.
errors.tooManyEmails: Add at most 50 people at a time.
errors.joinLinkInvalid: This join link is invalid or was turned off.
errors.transferToSelf: Choose someone else to make owner.
errors.transferToGuest: Make them a member before making them owner.
errors.twoFactorFirst: Turn on two-step verification for your own account first, or sign in with a passkey.

errors.tooManyRequests: Too many requests. Try again later.
errors.creationRestricted: Only the server's administrators can create workspaces.
errors.agentUser: This is an agent, not a person. Change or archive it in the agent's own settings.

security.description: Decide how people sign in, who can bring people into this workspace, what guests can do, what can leave it (exports, connected apps) and who can publish pages to the web. Only owners can change these settings.

requireTwoFactor.title: Require two-step verification
requireTwoFactor.description: Everyone must use an authenticator app or sign in with a passkey to open this workspace. People without either are asked to set one up first. Apps connected over MCP and REST API tokens are not affected.
requireTwoFactor.setUpFirst: Turn on two-step verification for your own account first.
requireTwoFactor.withoutCount: {count, plural, one {# person here hasn't set it up yet.} other {# people here haven't set it up yet.}}

accessRequests.title: Access requests
accessRequests.description: People who open a link to a page they can't see can ask for access, with a message. The people with full access to the page get the request. Off: they only see that they don't have access.

guestInvites.title: Who can invite guests
guestInvites.description: People outside the workspace join as guests when someone shares a page with them by email. They see only the pages shared with them.

guestPrivatePages.title: Guests can create private pages
guestPrivatePages.description: Guests can add pages at the top of the sidebar that only they can see, and share them like any page. Off: they only work in pages shared with them.

publishing.title: Who can publish to the web
publishing.description: Published pages can be read, and public forms filled in, by anyone with the link. Guests can never publish. Pages and forms already on the web stay there until someone turns them off. Off: nobody can publish, and pages, forms and the site already on the web stop working until publishing is turned back on.

publications.title: Published pages
publications.description: Every page of this workspace that is on the web. Owners can take any of them offline.
publications.privatePage: A page you don't have access to
publications.confirm: Unpublish this page? The link stops working for everyone.
publications.off: Publishing is turned off: none of these pages are on the web right now. They come back when publishing is turned on again, unless you unpublish them.

forms.title: Public forms
forms.description: Every form of this workspace that takes answers from the web. Owners can turn off any of them.
forms.empty: No forms take answers from the web.
forms.privateForm: A form you don't have access to
forms.name: {view} in {database}
forms.confirm: Turn off this form's public link? It stops working for everyone.
forms.stale: Takes no answers: whoever opened it lost access
forms.off: Publishing is turned off: none of these forms take answers right now. They come back when publishing is turned on again, unless you turn them off.

loginMethod.title: How members sign in
loginMethod.description: With single sign-on only, members must sign in through the identity provider to open this workspace. Owners and guests can still use any method, so a broken identity provider can't lock you out.
loginMethod.setUpFirst: Set up single sign-on below first.

sso.title: Single sign-on (SSO)
sso.description: Connect your organization's identity provider over OpenID Connect or SAML. People with an address in its verified domains can sign in with it; the first time, their account is created and they join as members.

setup.oidcRedirectUriHint: Add this as an allowed redirect (callback) URL of the client at your identity provider.

dns.body: To prove these domains are yours, add a TXT record for each at your DNS provider, then verify. Nobody can sign in with this connection until then.
dns.name: Name
dns.verified: Domains verified. Single sign-on is on.

form.issuerHint: The address its OpenID configuration is served under (…/.well-known/openid-configuration).
form.metadataKept: Leave empty to keep the stored metadata
form.certificateKept: Leave empty to keep the stored certificate
form.domainsHint: Separated by commas, for example example.com, example.org. Subdomains are included.

errors.invalidDomain: {detail} can't be used: enter your organization's own email domains (not public mail services like gmail.com).
errors.noDomains: Add at least one email domain.
errors.invalidIssuer: The issuer must be an https address.
errors.discoveryFailed: Couldn't read the provider's OpenID configuration at {detail}. Check the issuer address.
errors.invalidSaml: Paste the identity provider's metadata XML, or enter its SSO URL, entity ID and signing certificate.
errors.dnsMismatch: The TXT record for {detail} wasn't found or has a different value. DNS changes can take a while to show up.
errors.domainTaken: {detail} is already used for single sign-on elsewhere on this server.
errors.name: Give the token a name of at most 100 characters.
errors.limit: A workspace can have at most 20 SCIM tokens. Revoke one first.
errors.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can do this.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

scim.title: User provisioning (SCIM)
scim.description: Let your identity provider add, update and remove members, and manage member groups, over SCIM 2.0.
scim.managed: {count, plural, =0 {No one is managed over SCIM yet.} one {# person is managed over SCIM.} other {# people are managed over SCIM.}}
scim.tokensDescription: The identity provider sends one as a bearer token. Each works only for this workspace.

created.title: Copy your token
created.body: Paste it into your identity provider now. It won't be shown again.

errors.name: Give the token a name of at most 100 characters.
errors.limit: A workspace can have at most 20 SCIM tokens. Revoke one first.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.

trashRetention.title: Delete pages in the trash after
trashRetention.description: Pages that have been in the trash this long are deleted for good, with their subpages and files. The trash shows how many days each page has left.

historyRetention.title: Page history
historyRetention.description: Earlier versions of a page are kept for {days} days, up to {count} per page. Saved versions and versions from before a restore are kept for {keptDays} days, and the latest version of a page always stays.

memberInvites.title: Who can add members
memberInvites.description: Owners can always add people. Members add people as members, never as owners.

allowedDomains.title: Allowed email domains
allowedDomains.description: People with an address on these domains, subdomains included, can join without an invitation. Public mail services like gmail.com can't be added.
allowedDomains.verifiedByEmail: Only verified addresses join on their own: new accounts get a verification link by email.
allowedDomains.verifiedByProvider: Only verified addresses join on their own. This server doesn't send email, so only accounts from Google, GitHub or single sign-on count as verified.

domainJoin.title: When someone from these domains signs in
domainJoin.description: This happens once per person: someone who left or was removed doesn't come back on their own.

joinRequests.title: Who can ask to join
joinRequests.description: Requests wait in Settings > Members for an owner to approve or decline.
joinRequests.allowed_domains: People with an allowed email domain
joinRequests.linkHint: The join link then asks an owner instead of adding people right away.

export.title: Allow export
export.description: Everyone in the workspace can download pages as Markdown, CSV or ZIP and print them to PDF. Off: those options are gone for everyone, owners included.

connectedApps.title: Connected apps and API tokens
connectedApps.description: What AI assistants and other apps connected over MCP, and REST API tokens, may do in this workspace. They never get more than the person who connected them. With no access, the workspace is hidden from them.

audit.description: A record of who changed what in this workspace: members and roles, invitations, sharing, teamspaces and groups, settings, security, deletions, publishing, connected apps and exports. Only owners can see it.
audit.retention: Newest first. Events are kept for one year.

settingNames.publishing: Who can publish to the web
settingNames.trashRetentionDays: Delete pages in the trash after
settingNames.domainJoin: When someone from these domains signs in

values.allowed_domains: People with an allowed email domain

notifications.heading: Notifications
notifications.description: Choose what shows in your inbox and what also comes by email.
notifications.assignmentDescription: Someone assigns you to a person property in a database row.
notifications.shareDescription: Someone gives you access to a page.
notifications.commentDescription: Someone comments on a page you started a comment thread in or replied to.
notifications.mentionDescription: Someone mentions you on a page with @.
notifications.reminderDescription: A reminder you set on a date in a page is due.
notifications.accessRequestDescription: Someone asks for access to a page you have full access to.
notifications.mailOff: This server can't send email right now, so none go out.
notifications.joinRequestDescription: Someone asks to join a workspace you own, or a member asks to invite someone.
notifications.automationDescription: A database automation lets you know about a row someone added or changed.

site.description: Give this workspace's published pages one readable address, a home page and navigation between them.
site.heading: Site
site.notSetUp: This workspace has no site yet. Its published pages are reachable only through their own links.
site.slugHint: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, 3 to 40 characters.
site.titleHint: Shown at the top of every page of the site.
site.homeHint: The page the site's address opens. Only published pages can be picked.
site.confirmRemove: Take the site down? Its address stops working; each published page keeps its own link.
site.membersOnly: Only owners can change the site.
site.pagesDescription: Published pages the site lists, each with its subpages. Pages that aren't listed keep working through their own links but can't be reached from the site.
site.pagesEmpty: No pages are published yet. Publish a page from its Share menu first.
site.privatePage: A page you don't have access to

errors.tooShort: The address needs at least 3 characters.
errors.tooLong: The address can have at most 40 characters.
errors.invalid: Use lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens; start and end with a letter or number.
errors.reserved: This address is reserved. Pick another one.
errors.homeNotPublished: Pick a published page of this workspace that you can see.
errors.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can do this.

connections.heading: Connections
connections.description: Services your agents use: Slack, GitHub, a CRM, another Leafdesk… anything with a remote MCP server. Only owners see and manage them; which tools each agent may use is set on the agent. (Programs that use Leafdesk are under Security › Connected apps.)
connections.approvalNote: Agents run tools that only read at once. Every other call waits for an owner’s approval in the inbox; unanswered for a day, nothing is sent.

notices.signedIn: Signed in. The connection’s tools are listed below.
notices.oauthFailed: The sign-in didn’t finish. Try again; if it keeps failing, check the address and that the service allows Leafdesk to sign in.

errors.blocked: That address is on a private network, which connections can’t reach.
errors.notMcp: That address doesn’t answer as an MCP server.
errors.unauthorized: The server didn’t accept the sign-in.
errors.tokenForNewUrl: A new address needs its token: paste it again.
errors.invalidTrigger: Pick an agent of this workspace.
errors.oauthFailed: Signing in didn’t work. Try again.

approval.decided: Someone already answered this call, or it ran out of time.
approval.forbidden: Only owners can answer an agent’s call.

connections.addDescription: Enter the address of the service’s MCP server. Leafdesk keeps its credentials sealed on the server; they are never shown again.

fields.name: Name
fields.urlHelp: Its MCP endpoint, usually ending in /mcp. Only https addresses on the internet.

authHelp.oauth: You sign in at the service; Leafdesk registers itself and keeps the access it gets.
authHelp.token: Sent as a bearer token with every call.
authHelp.none: For servers that need no sign-in.

fields.tokenKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved one

presets.hmac: Leafdesk signature (Zapier, Make, n8n, your own)

statusErrors.unauthorized: The server didn’t accept the credentials. Sign in again or change the token.
statusErrors.notMcp: The address doesn’t answer as an MCP server.
statusErrors.timeout: The server took too long to answer.
statusErrors.oauth: Signing in didn’t work. Try again.
statusErrors.other: Something went wrong with this connection.

tools.description: Each tool is classed by what the server says of it: tools marked read-only run at once, all others wait for approval. Change a class if the server is wrong.
tools.notListed: Its tools are listed once the connection works.
tools.overridden: Classed by an owner, not as the server marked it

addressHelp.hmac: Send events here as POST requests signed with the secret below, the way Leafdesk’s own webhooks sign: X-Leafdesk-Signature is t=TIME,v1=HMAC (TIME in Unix seconds, HMAC the hex HMAC-SHA256 of TIME, a dot and the body), X-Leafdesk-Event names the type and X-Leafdesk-Delivery gives an id.
addressHelp.slack: Paste this as the Request URL of your Slack app’s Event Subscriptions, and paste the app’s signing secret below.
addressHelp.github: Add a webhook with this payload URL, content type application/json and the secret below.

events.triggersHelp: Which agent runs when an event arrives. An event type like “issues” also takes “issues.opened”; leave it empty for every event.
events.noAgents: Create an agent first, then choose it here.
events.promptPlaceholder: What the agent should do with the event

connections.reconnectNote: Changing the address or the sign-in signs the connection out; it is tried again when you save. A new address also needs the token again, lists its tools afresh and takes this connection's tools away from agents until you give them again.
connections.deleteBody: Its credentials, the tools agents had on it, its triggers and its events go with it. Calls waiting for approval fail without sending anything.

approval.notePlaceholder: Use the customer’s company name as the title
